---
title: "Easing, side by side"
description: "The same two-state animation under five easing curves, plus one with a separate easing for colour: six animated SVGs inlined on one page, each running on its own clock."
categories: [Animation]
image: figs/easing-poster.png
---



Easing decides how the interpolation fraction travels from 0 to 1 during a
transition. With `"linear"` it moves at a constant rate; the other curves start slowly,
end slowly, overshoot or bounce. `ease_aes()` sets it for a whole animation, and its
`position`, `color`, `size` and `alpha` arguments override it for one class of property.

`animate()` takes one plot, not a composition, so a comparison is several animations.
Here one helper builds the same scene, a dot that travels from one end of a track to the
other while its colour changes, once per easing:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
track <- data.frame(state = c("start", "end"), x = c(0, 10), y = 0, v = c(0, 1))

ease_demo <- function(ease, ..., title = ease) {
  vplot(track, width = 3.4, height = 1.4) |>
    mark_point(x = x, y = y, color = v, size = 3) |>
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 11), breaks = c(0, 5, 10)) |>
    scale_color_gradient(low = "#3a5a80", high = "#c1121f") |>
    guides(color = "none") |>
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()) |>
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) |>
    transition_states(state, transition_length = 3, state_length = 1) |>
    ease_aes(ease, ...) |>
    animate(nframes = 64, fps = 20)
}

demos <- list(
  linear         = ease_demo("linear"),
  cubic          = ease_demo("cubic-in-out"),
  back           = ease_demo("back-out"),
  elastic        = ease_demo("elastic-out"),
  bounce         = ease_demo("bounce-out"),
  bounce_colour  = ease_demo("bounce-out", color = "linear",
                             title = "bounce-out, color = \"linear\"")
)
```
:::


Every demo has the same timing (64 frames at 20 fps, so 3.2 s a loop, with the dot
held for a quarter of each half), so the six dots leave and arrive together and only the
path between differs:

- **linear**: constant speed, an abrupt start and stop.
- **cubic-in-out**: slow, fast, slow. The usual choice for things that should look
  like they have mass.
- **back-out**: runs a little past the end and comes back.
- **elastic-out**: overshoots several times, shrinking, like a spring.
- **bounce-out**: drops onto the end and bounces.

In all five the colour follows the same curve as the position, so the blue-to-red
change speeds up, slows down and bounces along with the dot. The last demo separates
them: `ease_aes("bounce-out", color = "linear")` keeps the bounce for position but
blends the colour evenly from blue to red. `position` always covers x and y together; there is one
positional curve per animation.

## Six animations, one page

These six SVGs are inlined into the page's HTML rather than linked as images, so their
styles share one document. Each animated SVG namespaces its CSS classes and keyframes
with a prefix derived from its own content, so the six step animations, and the
reduced-motion rule each one carries, do not override one another: every dot runs on
its own clock. The same holds when an animation is embedded with
`vellumwidget::as_widget()`, which also inlines the SVG.
